newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Retail stats strengthen case for lower NZD-Cullen.
newsitem.headline: Retail stats strengthen case for lower NZD-Cullen.

text.p: Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen said on Friday that weak retail trade figures for the September quarter would strengthen calls for a fall in the value of the New Zealand dollar.

"Results like this are going to make it harder for the Reserve Bank to continue justifying current monetary policy settings, they're another piece of evidence that the economy and consumer spending are slowing and certainly suggest there is some scope, to use the bank's language, for an easing in the very near future," Cullen said in a statement.
The benefits of such a move to exporters, manufacturers and farmers would be substantial.
It was Cullen's second statement in as many days calling for an easing of monetary policy.

Labour and the caretaker National Party government have both said they aim to lead the next government after inconclusive elections last month, and both are negotiating with the nationalist New Zealand First party on coalition possibilities.
